appraisal_events.evidence: Cette chanson... avait ravi... Mme Bontemps, laquelle entendit dire bientôt que c'était une ineptie... elle y substitua [une autre chanson] qui devint à son tour «une vieille rengaine de Massenet, dont la petite nous rebat les oreilles».
appraisal_events.explanation: Reported social opinion, relayed through the fickle Mme Bontemps, shifts from admiring to dismissing whatever song Albertine sings, ending in a quoted remark that mocks her as boring people with an old chestnut; the narrator's own opening line of fond indulgence toward Albertine's taste keeps this social verdict at ironic distance rather than fully endorsing it.

appraisal_events.evidence: nous pouvions parler tout en nous lavant chacun dans le nôtre, poursuivant une causerie... dans cette intimité que permet souvent à l'hôtel l'exiguïté du logement et le rapprochement des pièces, mais qui, à Paris, est si rare.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator frames the easy, continuous domestic closeness he shares with Albertine through the thin partition as a valued and rare intimacy, positively marking their bond.

status_effects.explanation: Albertine's musical taste and repertoire become a target of shifting, mocking social judgment, though the narrator's own affection blunts the force of this verdict.
The rare, easy domestic intimacy the narrator describes with Albertine casts her local emotional standing positively.
